b.d69fe00427:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Apocalýpsis beáti Ioánnis Apóstoli
<r>Apo 21:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Et vidi cælum novum et terram novam. Primum enim cælum, et prima terra ábiit, et mare iam non est.
<n>2</n> Et ego Ioánnes vidi sanctam civitátem Ierúsalem novam descendéntem de cælo a Deo, parátam sicut sponsam ornátam viro suo.
<n>3</n> Et audívi vocem magnam de throno dicéntem: Ecce tabernáculum Dei cum homínibus, et habitábit cum eis.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Dignus es, Dómine, accípere librum, et aperíre signácula eius, allelúia: quóniam occísus es, et redemísti nos Deo
* In sánguine tuo, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Fecísti enim nos Deo nostro regnum et sacerdótium.
<r>℟.</r> In sánguine tuo, allelúia.
b.76f113c5b0:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 1</h>
De libro Apocalýpsis beáti Joánnis Apóstoli
<r>Apo 21:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Et vidi cælum novum et terram novam. Primum enim cælum, et prima terra ábiit, et mare jam non est.
<n>2</n> Et ego Joánnes vidi sanctam civitátem Jerúsalem novam descendéntem de cælo a Deo, parátam sicut sponsam ornátam viro suo.
<n>3</n> Et audívi vocem magnam de throno dicéntem: Ecce tabernáculum Dei cum homínibus, et habitábit cum eis.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Thou art worthy, O Lord, to take the book, and to open the seals thereof; alleluia: because thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God,
* In thy blood, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> And hast made us to our God a kingdom and priests.
<r>℟.</r> In thy blood, alleluia.
b.b7e3050f61:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Ad gáudia paradísi perdúcat nos misericórdia Christi.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Apo 21:3-5</r>
<n>3</n> Et ipsi pópulus eius erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit eórum Deus:
<n>4</n> Et abstérget Deus omnem lácrymam ab óculis eórum: et mors ultra non erit, neque luctus, neque clamor, neque dolor erit ultra, quia prima abiérunt.
<n>5</n> Et dixit qui sedébat in throno: Ecce nova fácio ómnia.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Ego sicut vitis fructificávi suavitátem odóris, allelúia:
* Transíte ad me, omnes qui concupíscitis me, et a generatiónibus meis adimplémini, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Ego diligéntes me díligo; et qui mane vigiláverint ad me, invénient me.
<r>℟.</r> Transíte ad me, omnes qui concupíscitis me, et a generatiónibus meis adimplémini, allelúia, allelúia.
b.b75a2e24dd:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

<r>Apo 21:3-5</r>
<n>3</n> Et ipsi pópulus ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit eórum Deus:
<n>4</n> Et abstérget Deus omnem lácrymam ab óculis eórum: et mors ultra non erit, neque luctus, neque clamor, neque dolor erit ultra, quia prima abiérunt.
<n>5</n> Et dixit qui sedébat in throno: Ecce nova fácio ómnia.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> As the vine I have brought forth a pleasant odour, alleluia.
* Come over to me, all ye that desire me, and be filled with my fruits, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> I love them that love me: and they that in the morning early watch for me, shall find me.
<r>℟.</r> Come over to me, all ye that desire me, and be filled with my fruits, alleluia, alleluia.
b.ae80a6a0be:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<r>Apo 21:5-7</r>
<n>5</n> Et dixit mihi: Scribe, quia hæc verba fidelíssima sunt, et vera.
<n>6</n> Et dixit mihi: Factum est: ego sum Alpha et Oméga, inítium et finis. Ego sitiénti dabo de fonte aquæ vitæ, gratis.
<n>7</n> Qui vícerit, possidébit hæc: et ero illi Deus, et ille erit mihi fílius.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Audívi vocem de cælo, tamquam vocem tonítrui magni, allelúia: Regnábit Deus noster in ætérnum, allelúia:
* Quia facta est salus, et virtus, et potéstas Christi eius, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Et vox de throno exívit, dicens: Laudem dícite Deo nostro, omnes Sancti eius, et qui timétis Deum, pusílli et magni.
<r>℟.</r> Quia facta est salus, et virtus, et potéstas Christi eius, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Allelúia, allelúia.

b.341f2dd336:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>N</c>ono Kaléndas Maii Luna décima séptima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>N</h>atális sancti Geórgii Mártyris, cuius illústre martýrium inter Mártyrum corónas Ecclésia Dei venerátur.
<h>I</h>n vico Tenkítten, ad sinum Venédicum, in Borússia, item natális sancti Adalbérti, Epíscopi Pragénsis et Mártyris, qui Polónis et Húngaris Evangélium prædicávit.
<h>V</h>aléntiæ, in Gállia, pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Felícis Presbýteri, Fortunáti et Achilléi Diaconórum. Hi, cum fuíssent a beáto Irenǽo, Lugdunénsi Epíscopo, missi ad prædicándum verbum Dei, et máximam illíus civitátis partem ad Christi fidem convertíssent, a Duce Cornélio sunt in cárcerem trusi; deínde, diutíssime verberáti, cruribúsque confráctis, circa rotárum vertíginem stricti, fumum quoque in equúlei suspensióne perpéssi; ad extrémum gládio consummáti sunt.
<h>M</h>edioláni sancti Mároli, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>T</h>ulli, in Gállia, sancti Gerárdi, eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopi.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.d897878b5e:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>A</c>pril 23rd 2027, the 17th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:

<h>T</h>he holy martyr George, whose illustrious martyrdom, [in the year 303,] the church of God honours among the crowns of her martyrs.
<h>I</h>n Prussia, [in the year 997,] the holy martyr Adalbert, Bishop of Prague, who preached the Gospel to the Poles and Hungarians.
<h>A</h>t Valence, in Gaul, the holy martyrs the Priest Felix and the Deacons Fortunatus and Achilleus. They had been sent forth to preach the Word of God by blessed Irenaeus, Bishop of Lyon, and had brought a great part of the city of Valence to believe in Christ, when they were cast into prison by Cornelius the general. They were long beaten, their legs were broken, they were tied to the outside of turning wheels, hung in smoke upon the rack, and at length slain with the sword, [in the year 212.]
<h>A</h>t Milan, [in the year 423,] the holy Confessor Marolus, Bishop [of that see.]
<h>A</h>t Toul, in Gaul, holy Gerard, Bishop of that city, [in the year 994.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
